record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of finding the smallest-size training-set-consistent subset when the classification problem has exactly two classes?

evidence.quote: Wilfong [40] showed in 1991 that the problem of finding the smallest size training-set consistent subset is NP-complete when there are three or more classes. The complexity for the case of two classes remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane (or, more generally, in R^d for some d ≥ 2), and let c : P → {0, 1} be a 2-coloring of P (the two "classes"). A subset S ⊆ P is called training-set consistent (or a consistent subset) if, for every point p ∈ P, every nearest neighbor of p in S (with respect to Euclidean distance) has the same color as p. Equivalently, the nearest-neighbor classifier built from the labeled set (S, c|_S) correctly classifies every point of P.

The minimum consistent subset problem (MCS) asks, given (P, c), to determine a consistent subset S ⊆ P of smallest possible cardinality. It is known that for three or more color classes the corresponding decision problem ("is there a consistent subset of size at most k?") is NP-complete. 

Problem: Determine the computational complexity of the minimum consistent subset problem in the two-class case. Specifically, decide whether the decision version of MCS restricted to instances with exactly two colors is NP-complete, polynomial-time solvable, or of some intermediate complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-class case was settled by Khodamoradi, Krishnamurti, and Roy (WALCOM 2018, "Consistent Subset Problem with Two Labels"), who proved that the minimum consistent subset problem is NP-complete already for two-colored point sets in R^d for every d ≥ 2, via a reduction from planar rectilinear monotone 3-SAT. Subsequent work (e.g., Biniaz–Cabello–Maheshwari–Smid, Algorithmica 2021) cites this as the resolution of the open two-class case left by Wilfong (1991).

status_evidence.title: Consistent Subset Problem with Two Labels
status_evidence.snippet: The consistent subset problem with two colors is NP-complete in any dimension d ≥ 2, by reduction from planar rectilinear monotone 3-SAT.
status_evidence.claim: Two-class minimum consistent subset is NP-complete (Khodamoradi, Krishnamurti, Roy, 2018).

status_evidence.title: On the Minimum Consistent Subset Problem (arXiv:1810.09232)
status_evidence.snippet: This problem is known to be NP-complete even for two-colored point sets.
status_evidence.claim: The two-color case is acknowledged as NP-complete in subsequent literature.
